analysis.title: Tech Ain't Teflon, Gold Is Breaking, And The Dollar Won't Budge
key_insights: NDX is testing major long-term support, including the trendline from the Liberation Day lows and key levels from last year. It is well below the 200-day moving average, and the 21-day has crossed below the 200-day (a light death cross).
A similar cross earlier this year coincided with local lows. The same cross in March last year was followed by the Liberation Day sell-off.

Hedge funds are selling global tech at the fastest pace in a decade on a trailing six-week basis (-4.4 z-score). The global tech long/short ratio fell from a YTD peak of 2.9 to 1.79, near 10-year lows.
Fundamental long/short funds cut gross leverage by 4.4 points in November to 206.3% (23rd percentile over the past year). Net leverage fell 7.6 points to 41.6%, the lowest in five years.
Nomura estimates aggregate SPX dealer gamma at about -$7.3bn, near the bottom of its historical range. Dealer hedging can amplify moves in either direction.
McElligott sees the VIX floor shifting higher, but sees limited positioning fuel for a volatility shock above 30 without a much deeper equity selloff.
The current tech sell-off is tracking the autumn 2018 pattern closely. NDX lost about 25% from peak to the late-2018 lows.

TS Lombard notes the Nasdaq peaked on March 10, 2000 and lost more than a third by mid-April, while the S&P 500 stayed near record highs for six months. Broad market pressure arrived only when the economic outlook deteriorated.

In 2000, semiconductor sales kept rising and order backlogs stayed elevated after the Nasdaq peak. Within six months shortages turned into a glut, so strong fundamentals did not prevent further downside.
Gold is breaking below the trendline in place since 2024 and below the 100-week moving average for the first time since late 2023. RSI is oversold. The 200-week moving average is just above $3,000.
Gold ETF holdings rose 211 tonnes in Q3 (Europe 92 tonnes). ANZ warns North American ETF holdings could fall in Q4 as monetary conditions tighten.
The euro is weak and not catching a bid despite lower oil and gas prices this month.

The dollar is rising despite the tech sell-off and overshoots the widening in US rate differentials. Deutsche Bank's tracker of 100+ foreign-domiciled ETFs shows the largest two-week buying of US stocks this year, and DB questions whether that buying and widening rate differentials can both continue.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Gold has broken the 2024 trendline and the 100-week moving average. The 200-week average is the next long-term support.

US equity inflows from foreigners and widening rate differentials may not both continue if turmoil persists.

tension_points.bull_case: A similar death cross earlier this year coincided with local lows, and hedge fund positioning and leverage are already at multi-year extremes, so much risk has been removed.
tension_points.bear_case: The 2018 pattern (about 25% peak-to-trough) and the 2000 experience show that strong fundamentals do not prevent further downside. Orders and backlogs took months to adjust before shortages turned into a glut.
tension_points.what_invalidates: NDX breaking the long-term trendline from the Liberation Day lows and last year's key levels.

tension_points.bull_case: Foreigners are buying US equities aggressively (the largest two-week buying spree this year in DB's ETF tracker) and rate differentials are widening, both supporting the dollar.
tension_points.bear_case: DB questions whether the equity buying and widening rate differentials can both continue if market turmoil persists.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Market turmoil persisting, which would break one of the two supports.
